Jonas — thanks again for the demo last week. CloudPivot loved the latency profile and the roadmap notes on private deployments. Before we move toward a signed commercial sheet, our legal/commercial team asked for clarity on two items that will affect our internal approval: 1) whether you require a holdback / escrow on the first-year revenue for co-sell deals; and 2) the exact mechanics and window for lead registration (to avoid duplicate-credit disputes).

We put together a quick sketch of what we typically accept on our side (attached) but would like to align on Redwood's preference so our finance folks can model payouts. High level asks:
- Holdback: do you propose a % of first-year commission withheld for x months to protect against early churn/clawbacks? If so, what's the percentage and release cadence?
- Registration: our sellers register opportunities in our partner portal; we need a clear timeframe (e.g., 60/90 days) and the minimum technical qualification for auto-approval.

Can you and your partner ops leads share a proposal? Happy to set a short call if faster.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Strategic Alliances | CloudPivot Solutions

Samantha — thanks for the clear asks and the attachment. Looping in Camila (Partner Ops) and Ben (Rev) who run this at Redwood. Quick summary of where we usually land and why:

- Holdback / escrow: Redwood typically withholds 15% of our commissionable payout for the initial 6 months after customer go-live. The holdback exists to protect against de-bookings and early churn. Release cadence is: 50% of the holdback at month 6, remaining 50% at month 12 assuming no clawback events. Clawback triggers: contract cancellation, fraud, or material breach.

- Registration window: partner-initiated registration is accepted if the customer signs within 90 days of registration and the partner owns primary sales contact. Technical minimums for auto-approval: product demo completed (recording link), identified use case, and nominated Redwood technical champion. We also accept exceptions via manual review.

We can be flexible on the % and timing for strategic pilots — happy to propose a concession for your first three joint customers (reduce holdback to 8% with release at month 9) if CloudPivot commits to a co-branded case study.

I'll let Camila share the operational details and the DocuSign-ready term sheet. If that looks good, we can route a one-page amendment through legal.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Alliances | Redwood Inference

The appendix is intentionally lightweight: demo recording, logo permission, and the lead's company domain + primary contact.

Operational notes (for your ops team):
- Registration path: partner-portal -> new registration -> attach demo link + contact -> auto-approve (90d) or manual review (if missing evidence).
- If a second partner attempts to register the same opportunity, system creates a contested registration and our ops team opens a 5-business-day adjudication window, during which both partners can submit evidence.
- Commission cadence: Redwood pays partner commission on a quarterly basis following invoice collection. For the holdback portion, once released the corresponding payout is included in the next quarterly run.

Samantha — quick answers from rev ops:
1) Expansion revenue: treated as new commissionable ARR for commission purposes. No holdback on expansions unless the expansion is within 60 days of cancellation of prior contract or there is evidence of churn risk. Essentially, we don't holdback routine expansion gear.
2) Contested registrations: yes, supplementary evidence (meeting recording, timestamped email thread, demo recording) is strongly preferred and will be accepted. We log evidence in the adjudication ticket and make a decision within the 5-business-day window.

If that aligns, Camila will update the DocuSign comments and we can route for signatures. Looking forward to the co-sell.
